newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa better but not out of danger.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa better but not out of danger.

text.p: Mother Teresa, fighting heart, lung and kidney problems, was much better on Monday but not out of danger after coronary artery surgery, her chief doctor said.
"She is much better than yesterday. She had a good sleep. But she is still not out of danger," the doctor, D.P. Shetty, told Reuters from Calcutta's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre.
Shetty said late on Sunday the 86-year-old Roman Catholic nun's heart pacemaker, fitted in 1989, had been reprogrammed to boost cardiac output to allow her kidneys to function better.
"She is still critically ill. You have to understand she has got a problem with her heart, kidney and lung," he added. "We are trying to take care of everything. She is stable."
Doctors have said long-standing lung and renal problems could complicate the nun's heart condition and recovery.
Mother Teresa, known as the "Saint of the Gutters" for her devotion to the poor, destitute and dying, had surgery to clear two coronary artery blockages at the Calcutta clinic on Friday.
Mother Teresa, born of Albanian parents as Gonxhe Bojaxhi, was moved to the clinic last Tuesday after entering the nearby Woodlands Nursing Home on November 22.
